audit_result.proof_trace: The cookie client (anon key + user JWT, RLS enforced) is used for admin UPDATE/DELETE operations on arbitrary users' rows in toggleAdminStatus, deleteMember, updateMemberAdmin, and updateMemberTeams — but updateMyProfile uses supabaseAdmin for own-row updates, confirming RLS blocks authenticated-role UPDATEs on the members table. This creates a binary gap: either admin mutations silently fail with 0 rows affected (app returns success while nothing changes), OR the RLS policy allows admin-conditional cross-row UPDATE, in which case an attacker with a valid JWT can call the Supabase REST API directly to set is_admin=true on their own row if column-level security on is_admin is absent.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An authenticated user calls PATCH /rest/v1/members?supabase_auth_user_id=eq.<their-id> with Authorization: Bearer <user_jwt> and body {is_admin: true} directly against the Supabase REST endpoint — bypassing all app-level admin checks — and gains admin-level RLS access if the members table UPDATE policy allows authenticated users to modify their own is_admin field.

PROP-stem-system-asm-001.text: Supabase RLS policies correctly enforce row-level access for cookie-based (non-admin) client.
